papers.title: Detecting and Preventing Data Poisoning Attacks on AI Models
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the critical issue of data poisoning attacks on AI models, a growing concern in the ever-evolving landscape of artificial intelligence and cybersecurity. As advanced technology systems become increasingly prevalent across various sectors, the need for robust defence mechanisms against adversarial attacks becomes paramount. The study aims to develop and evaluate novel techniques for detecting and preventing data poisoning attacks, focusing on both theoretical frameworks and practical applications. Through a comprehensive literature review, experimental validation using the CIFAR-10 and Insurance Claims datasets, and the development of innovative algorithms, this paper seeks to enhance the resilience of AI models against malicious data manipulation. The study explores various methods, including anomaly detection, robust optimization strategies, and ensemble learning, to identify and mitigate the effects of poisoned data during model training. Experimental results indicate that data poisoning significantly degrades model performance, reducing classification accuracy by up to 27 % in image recognition tasks (CIFAR-10) and 22 % in fraud detection models (Insurance Claims dataset). The proposed defence mechanisms, including statistical anomaly detection and adversarial training, successfully mitigated poisoning effects, improving model robustness and restoring accuracy levels by an average of $15-20 \%$. The findings further demonstrate that ensemble learning techniques provide an additional layer of resilience, reducing false positives and false negatives caused by adversarial data injections. The findings of this paper contribute to the broader understanding of adversarial machine learning and provide actionable insights for practitioners in industries facing emerging threats to AI-based systems. By addressing the challenges of data poisoning attacks, this study aims to improve the security and reliability of AI models, ultimately fostering greater trust in AI technologies across critical applications.

papers.title: Robust and Adaptive Dual-Defense Framework Against Data Poisoning Attacks in Recommendation Systems
papers.abstract: Deep learning-based recommendation systems are highly vulnerable to data poisoning attacks, where adversaries manipulate user interactions to degrade model integrity. We hypothesize that combining an active robust loss with a passive GAN-based detection will significantly reduce poisoning impact in recommendation systems without sacrificing utility. We propose a robust and adaptive dual-defense framework: the active defense integrates a crafted loss function to mitigate poisoning effects while maintaining model performance. The passive defense employs a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)-based detection model to identify and filter poisoned data, enhancing detection accuracy and system security. The framework supports classical matrix factorization (MF) model and large language model (LLM)-based pipelines and scales to large datasets. Extensive experiments across multiple real-world datasets at varying poison rates show that our method outperforms representative defenses, consistently reducing attack success without sacrificing recommendation quality. The framework also admits a federated instantiation, where robust training and GAN-based detection run on clients and only privacy-preserving summaries are aggregated. The proposed method significantly improves the robustness and adaptability of recommendation systems under data poisoning attacks.

papers.title: Adaptive AI-Driven Learning Architecture for Real Time Detection and Prevention of Data Poisoning and Model Evasion Attacks
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been integrated into cybersecurity systems particularly in cyber threat intelligence (CTI) and has significantly enhanced the detection, analysis, and mitigation of sophisticated cyber threats in real time in organisations. Unlike traditional static defence mechanisms, which rely on fixed rules or offline retraining, the proposed architecture empowers continuous dynamic learning capabilities to identify and mitigate attacks as they unfold ensuring the integrity and reliability of AI-driven CTI systems. AI models to self-heal and harden against evolving adversarial tactics. The primary goal is to enhance CTI operations by providing timely, accurate threat detection and robust mitigation thereby reducing the window of opportunity for attackers and improving overall cybersecurity posture. This article presents a comprehensive adaptive learning architecture with formalised threat models, architectural specifications, and empirical validation. Experimental evaluation using benchmark datasets (CIC-IDS2017 and VirusTotal) demonstrates that the system achieves 43.7% higher evasion detection accuracy than traditional static anomaly detectors, while maintaining processing latency below 5 milliseconds. The architecture successfully detects 89.1% of poisoning attacks and reduces false positive rates by 37.5% relative to baseline methods. The key contributions of this article include the design of an integrated adaptive learning system that simultaneously detects and prevents both data poisoning and model evasion attacks within cybersecurity AI models.

papers.title: Resilient Autonomy: Securing Intelligent Systems Against Adversarial Attacks
papers.abstract: As autonomous systems become central to mission-critical operations, their ability to withstand adversarial threats is crucial to ensuring trust, safety, and uninterrupted functionality. This paper introduces a comprehensive framework for resilient autonomy that proactively prevents, detects, and mitigates key adversarial challenges, including sensor spoofing, sensor manipulation, and machine learning model poisoning. We present a layered defense architecture that integrates adversarial robust learning, real-time anomaly detection, and secure control strategies to maintain reliable autonomous behavior in compromised environments. Our hybrid resilience model addresses both inference-time perturbations and upstream vulnerabilities in data acquisition and processing pipelines. The system employs adaptive decision logic and decentralized failover mechanisms to dynamically reconfigure operations upon detection of anomalies or suspicious behavior, thus preserving mission continuity. In addition, we embed explainable AI modules to enhance transparency, facilitate system diagnostics, and support operator trust. We validate the proposed framework using a suite of simulated adversarial scenarios across diverse autonomous agents, including drones, mobile robots, and vehicle models. Results demonstrate significant gains in threat resistance, operational stability, and recovery time when compared to conventional defenses. This work lays the foundation for building self-reliant, attack-aware autonomous systems that are capable of sustaining functionality under adversarial uncertainty.

summary: The literature reveals a focused investigation into defensive strategies against data poisoning and adversarial attacks, emphasizing the development of robust frameworks that enhance AI resilience, particularly in recommendation systems and autonomous systems. Key contributions include novel detection techniques, dual-defense mechanisms, and adaptive learning architectures, though limitations exist regarding scalability, generalizability, and real-world applicability. Gaps identified suggest a need for continuous adaptive learning and comprehensive evaluations of defense mechanisms across diverse AI applications, highlighting the importance of integrating explainable AI for improved security and trustworthiness.
scholarly_positioning: Current literature predominantly addresses defensive strategies against data poisoning and adversarial attacks, yet significant gaps remain in scalability and adaptability of these methods across diverse AI applications. While existing frameworks, such as dual-defense mechanisms and robust adversarial training, show promise, they often lack empirical validation in dynamic environments and fail to account for evolving attack vectors. This research proposes a novel adaptive learning architecture that integrates real-time anomaly detection and robust optimization, aiming to enhance resilience in both recommendation systems and autonomous systems. By addressing the limitations of prior work, particularly the need for comprehensive evaluations and generalizable solutions, this study seeks to contribute to a deeper understanding of AI security and the development of more robust systems capable of withstanding sophisticated adversarial threats.
research_scope: This study will investigate the effectiveness of a novel adaptive learning architecture designed to enhance the resilience of recommendation systems and autonomous systems against data poisoning and adversarial attacks. The evaluation period will span six months, during which the architecture will be tested against various attack vectors using datasets such as CIFAR-10 and Insurance Claims. The primary outcomes will include detection accuracy and model performance, while secondary outcomes will assess robustness against different types of attacks and response times. The study will compare the proposed architecture against existing dual-defense frameworks and robust adversarial training techniques to establish baseline effectiveness. Controls will ensure consistent model architectures and training protocols, while ablation studies will explore the impact of specific defense components on overall system performance.

technical_feasibility: The study requires access to labeled datasets such as CIFAR-10 and Insurance Claims, which are publicly available. It does not require hidden state extraction or open-source model access, as it focuses on model performance evaluation against existing frameworks. However, it may benefit from GPU resources for training and testing the models effectively. Since user trust is not directly studied, human participants or ethics approval are not necessary. The design is feasible as it stands, but ensuring adequate computational resources for model training and testing is crucial.
gap: Prior studies have demonstrated effective defensive strategies against data poisoning in recommendation systems; however, they treat the adaptability of these methods to evolving attack vectors as fixed, leaving unclear whether the proposed dual-defense frameworks can maintain performance in dynamic environments. This matters practically because the landscape of adversarial threats is constantly changing, necessitating systems that can adapt in real-time. Therefore, this study investigates the implementation of a novel adaptive learning architecture that integrates real-time anomaly detection and robust optimization to enhance resilience against data poisoning and adversarial attacks in both recommendation systems and autonomous systems.
question: How does the implementation of a novel adaptive learning architecture for real-time anomaly detection and robust optimization enhance the resilience of recommendation systems and autonomous systems against evolving data poisoning and adversarial attacks compared to existing dual-defense frameworks and robust adversarial training techniques, in terms of detection accuracy and model performance?
theoretical_mechanism: The proposed adaptive learning architecture serves as the independent variable, which enhances AI resilience against data poisoning and adversarial attacks (dependent variable) through real-time anomaly detection and robust optimization (mediators). The theoretical framework is based on adaptive systems theory, positing that continuous learning and adjustment to environmental changes improve system performance. The causal chain begins with the architecture's ability to detect anomalies, which triggers adaptive responses that optimize model performance and robustness. System-level outcomes, such as reduced attack success rates and improved detection accuracy, are mediated by technical mechanisms like anomaly detection filters and robust optimization strategies. User-level outcomes, including user satisfaction and perceived reliability, are influenced by the system's performance and transparency in its decision-making processes. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the effectiveness of real-time adaptations and the stability of model performance across diverse attack vectors.
hypothesis: The implementation of a novel adaptive learning architecture for real-time anomaly detection will result in significantly higher detection accuracy compared to existing dual-defense frameworks, thereby enhancing the resilience of recommendation systems and autonomous systems against data poisoning and adversarial attacks.

proposal: This research proposal aims to develop a novel adaptive learning architecture that enhances the resilience of AI systems, specifically recommendation systems and autonomous systems, against evolving data poisoning and adversarial attacks. Unlike existing dual-defense frameworks and robust adversarial training techniques, which often lack adaptability in dynamic environments, this architecture integrates real-time anomaly detection and robust optimization to continuously adjust to new attack vectors. The literature reveals significant gaps in the scalability and adaptability of current defensive strategies, particularly their inability to maintain performance under evolving adversarial conditions, as highlighted by the limitations of prior studies that focus on static datasets and fixed attack types. This study will operationalize constructs such as 'detection accuracy' (measured as the percentage of correctly identified attacks) and 'robustness' (assessed through attack success rates) using publicly available datasets like CIFAR-10 and Insurance Claims, ensuring reproducibility through consistent training protocols and fixed model architectures. The methodology includes comparative evaluations against established baselines, such as existing dual-defense frameworks, with ablation studies to assess the impact of specific defense components. Statistical analyses will validate improvements in detection accuracy and resilience, addressing potential confounds like dataset variability and resource constraints. The theoretical mechanism posits that the adaptive architecture (independent variable) enhances detection accuracy and resilience (dependent variables) through robust optimization (mediator), leading to reduced attack success rates and increased user trust. This research is expected to contribute to the theoretical framework of adaptive systems theory in AI security, provide empirical insights into the effectiveness of adaptive learning in dynamic environments, and offer practical guidelines for deploying resilient AI systems in real-world applications. Key limitations include potential generalization issues to unseen attack types and the need for performance validation in resource-constrained environments, alongside risks of misinterpretation of results. Overall, this study seeks to advance scientific understanding of AI resilience by demonstrating how adaptive learning mechanisms can effectively counter sophisticated adversarial threats.

Major weaknesses: The proposal lacks a detailed explanation of how the proposed mechanisms will specifically address the identified problems, leading to some unsupported assumptions. Next band requirements: Incorporating more empirical justification for assumptions and clearly linking the theoretical mechanisms to expected outcomes would strengthen coherence.

rubric_scores.level: 15-17: clear novelty with meaningful research differentiation
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal introduces a novel adaptive learning architecture that aims to enhance AI resilience, which is a meaningful advancement over existing frameworks. It identifies significant gaps in current literature and proposes a concrete mechanism for improvement. Major weaknesses: While the novelty is clear, the proposal could better articulate how this architecture fundamentally differs from existing methods beyond just being adaptive. Next band requirements: To achieve a higher score, the proposal should explicitly detail the unique theoretical contributions and how they advance the field beyond existing frameworks.

The methodology is generally sound, with a clear plan for evaluation against established baselines. However, it lacks detailed statistical analysis plans and risk mitigation strategies for potential confounds. Major weaknesses: The proposal does not sufficiently address how it will control for confounding variables or provide a comprehensive risk analysis for the experimental design. Next band requirements: Incorporating a more robust statistical analysis plan and detailed controls for confounding variables would enhance methodological rigor.

rubric_scores.level: 12-13: strong literature grounding with good comparative analysis
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal engages with relevant literature and identifies gaps effectively. However, it primarily summarizes existing work without deeply critiquing methodologies or identifying unresolved tensions. Major weaknesses: The literature review lacks a critical synthesis that compares methodologies and highlights specific shortcomings in existing approaches. Next band requirements: To improve, the proposal should provide a more in-depth critique of existing literature and articulate how the proposed research addresses specific unresolved issues.

rubric_scores.level: 7-8: approaching PhD-level with some shallow areas
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal demonstrates a reasonable level of theoretical sophistication but lacks depth in discussing the mechanisms and limitations of the proposed architecture. Major weaknesses: There is insufficient discussion of the theoretical implications of the findings and the broader impact on the field. Next band requirements: Enhancing the discussion of theoretical implications and limitations would elevate the academic depth of the proposal.

The proposal is generally well-written and organized, with a clear academic tone. However, some sections could benefit from greater conciseness and precision. Major weaknesses: There are instances of redundancy and imprecision in terminology that could detract from clarity. Next band requirements: Improving conciseness and ensuring precise terminology throughout the proposal would enhance overall communication quality.

evaluation.comments: Total score: 78.0/100. Academic level: Master's-level. Major strengths: Clear identification of research gaps in AI resilience.; Proposed novel adaptive learning architecture with potential for significant impact.; Strong engagement with relevant literature. Major weaknesses: Insufficient operationalization of key concepts.; Lack of empirical justification for assumptions.; Limited critical analysis of existing methodologies. Required improvements for true PhD-level quality: Enhance operational definitions of constructs.; Provide empirical justification for theoretical claims.; Deepen the critique of existing literature and methodologies. Final verdict: The proposal demonstrates potential for PhD-level research but requires significant improvements in theoretical depth, methodological rigor, and critical engagement with existing literature to achieve genuine PhD-level maturity.
